title: There Is No Other God That Can Deliver
sections: I can trust in the Lord when my faith is tried
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints is the kingdom of God on earth
Jesus Christ is the Son of the Eternal Father

sayings.text: I fear my lord the king, who hath appointed your meat and your drink
sayings.speaker: The prince of the eunuchs
sayings.why: He was afraid the king would see Daniel’s group looking worse than the others. Daniel answered with a ten-day test (Daniel 1:12).

sayings.text: There is not a man upon the earth that can shew the king’s matter
sayings.speaker: The Chaldeans, to the king
sayings.why: The king’s wise men said no one could tell a king his own dream. Daniel answered that “there is a God in heaven that revealeth secrets” (Daniel 2:28).

sayings.text: I have found a man of the captives of Judah, that will make known unto the king the interpretation.
sayings.speaker: Arioch, the king’s captain
sayings.why: Arioch hurried Daniel in to the king as if he had found him himself. Really, Daniel had asked to be taken in (Daniel 2:24).

sayings.text: our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace
sayings.speaker: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego
sayings.why: Then they added, “But if not” (Daniel 3:18): even if God didn’t save them, they still would not worship the king’s image.

sayings.text: Did not we cast three men bound into the midst of the fire?
sayings.speaker: King Nebuchadnezzar
sayings.why: The astonished king jumped up. He saw four men walking free in the fire, and “they have no hurt” (Daniel 3:25).

sayings.text: Is not this great Babylon, that I have built for the house of the kingdom by the might of my power
sayings.speaker: Nebuchadnezzar, bragging
sayings.why: While the words were still in his mouth, a voice from heaven said, “The kingdom is departed from thee” (Daniel 4:31).

sayings.text: Let thy gifts be to thyself, and give thy rewards to another
sayings.speaker: Daniel, to Belshazzar
sayings.why: Belshazzar offered scarlet clothes, a gold chain and a high office. Daniel didn’t want them, but he read the writing anyway.

sayings.text: Thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee.
sayings.speaker: King Darius, to Daniel
sayings.why: Darius had been tricked into his own law. Early the next morning he called out, “is thy God… able to deliver thee from the lions?” (Daniel 6:20).

sayings.text: My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me
sayings.speaker: Daniel, from the den
sayings.why: Daniel had done no wrong before God or the king. He came out with “no manner of hurt” (Daniel 6:23), because he believed in his God.

words.clue: shall the God of heaven set up a ____, which shall never be destroyed
words.mean: God’s latter-day kingdom, His Church, will never be destroyed or given to anyone else.

words.clue: let them give us ____ to eat, and water to drink
words.mean: Daniel asked for simple food from seeds and grains, and God blessed him for keeping His law.

words.clue: a ____ was cut out without hands
words.mean: The stone cut out without hands is God’s kingdom, set up by Him and not by people.

words.clue: our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery ____
words.mean: The three friends knew God could save them from the fire, and they trusted Him either way.

words.clue: those that walk in ____ he is able to abase
words.mean: God can humble the proud, even the mightiest king on earth. Nebuchadnezzar learned it the hard way.

words.clue: Thou art ____ in the balances, and art found wanting
words.mean: God measured King Belshazzar’s life, and it didn’t measure up.

words.clue: one like the Son of man came with the ____ of heaven
words.mean: Daniel saw Jesus Christ, the Son of Man, coming in glory to receive a kingdom that lasts forever.

deep.intro: The lesson asks how Daniel and his friends answered pressure to do wrong (Daniel 1:10–13). The official in charge of their food was under pressure too.
deep.q: In Daniel 1:10, what did the prince of the eunuchs say Daniel’s plan would put in danger?
deep.hunt: In Daniel 1, what did the prince of the eunuchs say Daniel’s plan would put in danger?
deep.right: His own head, with the king
wrong: His job in the king’s kitchen
deep.why: Verse 10: “then shall ye make me endanger my head to the king.” So Daniel offered a fair ten-day test that wouldn’t get him in trouble.
deep.find: then shall ye make me endanger my head to the king

deep.intro: The lesson invites you to read the descriptions of the stone in Daniel 2:34–35. Here is the whole dream, right up to the moment the stone strikes.
deep.q: In Daniel 2:35, what did the broken pieces of the image become like?
deep.hunt: In Daniel 2, what did the broken pieces of the image become like?
wrong: Sand on the shore of the sea
Dust on a busy city street
deep.why: Verse 35: they “became like the chaff of the summer threshingfloors; and the wind carried them away.” Chaff is the dry husk that blows off grain.
deep.find: became like the chaff of the summer threshingfloors

deep.intro: The lesson asks what you can learn from Daniel’s words after he received the Lord’s help. Before he went to the king, he praised God.
deep.q: In Daniel 2:22, what does Daniel say dwells with God?
deep.hunt: In Daniel 2, what does Daniel say dwells with God?
deep.why: Verse 22: “he knoweth what is in the darkness, and the light dwelleth with him.” God sees what is hidden, and He gives light to those who ask.

deep.intro: The lesson points to Moses 6:57 to help explain Daniel 7:13–14. It tells where the title Son of Man comes from.
deep.q: In Moses 6:57, what is Heavenly Father’s name in the language of Adam?
deep.hunt: In Moses 6, what is Heavenly Father’s name in the language of Adam?
deep.why: Verse 57: “in the language of Adam, Man of Holiness is his name, and the name of his Only Begotten is the Son of Man.” So Son of Man means Son of the Man of Holiness.

deep.title: From the children’s part of the lesson
deep.intro: The children’s part of this week’s lesson starts with Daniel 1, 3 and 6. One idea is to share times you were blessed for making a good choice when it was hard.
deep.q: Which hymn does the lesson suggest singing together after you share those times?
deep.why: It suggests singing Choose the Right, number 239 in the hymnbook, after sharing how you have been blessed for making the right choice even when it was hard.

deep.title: From the Friend
deep.intro: The October Friend retells the story of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego for children. Read it, then look for what it says about who was in the fire.
deep.q: In the Friend’s retelling, what was the king surprised to see in the fire with the three men?
deep.why: The Friend says the king was surprised to see a heavenly being in the fire with them. Daniel 3:25 says the fourth was like the Son of God.
deep.find: a heavenly being in the fire with the three men

reels.hook: The king’s food was free. Daniel still said no.
reels.seek: A young captive decides not to eat the ruler’s dinner
reels.body: Daniel and his friends were taken to Babylon as young men to serve King Nebuchadnezzar. The king gave them his own rich food and wine, but Daniel “purposed in his heart” not to defile himself with it. He asked for ten days of plain food and water instead. The lesson invites you to compare the blessings that followed with those the Lord promises for keeping the Word of Wisdom (Doctrine and Covenants 89:18–21).

verse.text: But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king's meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.

question.q: What did Daniel do about the king’s food?
question.right: Asked kindly for a test of plain food
wrong: Ate a little so nobody would notice
Hid the food and pretended to eat it
question.why: Verse 8: he “requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.” He had already decided, so he asked politely for another way.

bonus.q: This week’s Scripture Helps give one reason the king’s food could defile Daniel. What might have been done with it first?
bonus.right: It was offered to Babylonian gods
wrong: It was cooked by enemy soldiers
It was taken from the temple
bonus.why: They say the king’s meat and wine may have been offered to Babylon’s gods first, so eating them would have been like joining in idol worship.
bonus.find: may have first been offered to Babylonian gods

image.alt: The blue-tiled Ishtar Gate of ancient Babylon, rebuilt inside the Pergamon Museum in Berlin
image.credit: Babylon's Ishtar Gate, about 575 BC. Photo: Kurt Kaiser, public domain

reels.hook: Where did the smartest students in Babylon get it?
reels.body: After three years of training, the king tested his young students himself. Daniel and his friends were “ten times better than all the magicians and astrologers” (Daniel 1:20). Where did that come from? Verse 17 says God gave it to them. The lesson asks what this teaches about how God prepared Daniel. Long before the king’s scary dream in chapter 2, God was already giving Daniel understanding of visions and dreams.

verse.text: As for these four children, God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom: and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.

question.q: Where did Daniel and his friends get their knowledge and skill?
question.why: Verse 17: “God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom.” Their training mattered, but the real gift came from God.

bonus.q: In Daniel 1:21, until whose first year did Daniel continue?
bonus.hunt: In Daniel 1, until whose first year did Daniel continue?
bonus.why: Verse 21: “Daniel continued even unto the first year of king Cyrus.” He served in Babylon through many kings and many years.
bonus.find: unto the first year of king Cyrus

image.alt: Illustration of the king, seen from behind, watching young Daniel and his friends study in a palace courtyard, one writing with a quill pen while another holds a scroll
image.credit: Old Testament Stories: Daniel and His Friends, from the Church Media Library

reels.hook: The king wants them dead. First, Daniel’s friends pray.
reels.body: The king ordered every wise man in Babylon killed, Daniel too. Daniel didn’t panic. He went to the king, then home to his three friends. Together they asked “the God of heaven” to be merciful (verse 18). That night God showed Daniel the secret in a vision. Before rushing to the king, Daniel stopped to thank Him (Daniel 2:20–23). They prepared, and God answered.

verse.text: That they would desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning this secret; that Daniel and his fellows should not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.

question.q: What did Daniel do before he gave the king an answer?
question.right: Prayed with his friends, then thanked God
wrong: Asked the other wise men to guess
Hid until the angry king calmed down
question.why: They asked to “desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning this secret.” When the answer came, Daniel blessed God before going in (Daniel 2:19).

bonus.q: In Daniel 2:14, how did Daniel answer Arioch, the captain sent to kill the wise men?
bonus.hunt: In Daniel 2, how did Daniel answer Arioch, the captain sent to kill the wise men?
bonus.why: Verse 14: “Daniel answered with counsel and wisdom to Arioch.” He stayed calm and wise, even with his life in danger.

image.alt: Drawing of two hands pressed together in prayer, in fine white lines on blue paper
image.credit: Praying Hands, by Albrecht Dürer, 1508. Public domain

reels.hook: He could have taken the credit. He gave it to God.
reels.body: The king asked Daniel if he could tell him “the dream which I have seen” (Daniel 2:26). Daniel could have taken the credit. Instead he said no wise man could do it, but God could. The secret came, he said, not “for any wisdom that I have more than any living” (Daniel 2:30). He wanted the king to know God, not to think Daniel was special.

verse.text: But there is a God in heaven that revealeth secrets, and maketh known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Thy dream, and the visions of thy head upon thy bed, are these;

question.q: Why could Daniel tell the king his dream?
question.right: God in heaven revealed it to him
wrong: He was wiser than all other men
He had studied the king’s dreams
question.why: “There is a God in heaven that revealeth secrets.” Daniel told the king the answer came from God, not from his own wisdom.

bonus.q: In Daniel 2:47, what does the king call Daniel’s God, besides a revealer of secrets?
bonus.hunt: In Daniel 2, what does the king call Daniel’s God, besides a revealer of secrets?
bonus.right: A God of gods and Lord of kings
wrong: The King of the whole earth
The Lord of all the heavens
bonus.why: Verse 47: “your God is a God of gods, and a Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets.” Daniel’s humility helped the king honor God.
bonus.find: a God of gods, and a Lord of kings

image.alt: Painting of young Daniel in white, kneeling before King Nebuchadnezzar on his throne and telling him his dream, as the dream’s great metal statue glows beside the king
image.credit: Daniel Interprets Nebuchadnezzar’s Dream, by Grant Romney Clawson

reels.hook: A little rock that grows until it covers the world.
reels.seek: God starts a reign that nobody will wipe out
reels.body: In the king’s dream, a stone “cut out without hands” (Daniel 2:34) smashed a giant statue of metal and clay. Then it became a great mountain and “filled the whole earth” (Daniel 2:35). Without hands means God made it, not people. President D. Todd Christofferson taught that this kingdom is The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, rolling forth to fill the earth.

verse.text: And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.

question.q: What does the stone in the king’s dream stand for?
question.why: Daniel said “the God of heaven” would “set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed.” Latter-day prophets teach that kingdom is the restored Church.

bonus.q: In D&C 65:2, what does the Lord say will roll forth unto the ends of the earth?
bonus.hunt: In D&C 65, what does the Lord say will roll forth unto the ends of the earth?
bonus.why: Verse 2: “from thence shall the gospel roll forth unto the ends of the earth, as the stone which is cut out of the mountain without hands.”
bonus.find: shall the gospel roll forth unto the ends of the earth

bonus.q: Does the stone filling the whole earth mean that everyone will join the Church, says the seminary manual?
bonus.right: No, it will spread across the earth
wrong: Yes, every person will join it
Yes, but only after a thousand years
bonus.why: The manual explains it doesn’t mean everyone will join. It means the Church will spread throughout the earth, as Nephi also saw.
bonus.find: does not mean that everyone will join the Lord’s Church

image.alt: The whole Earth seen from space, a blue and white ball against black
image.credit: The Blue Marble, Earth from Apollo 17, 1972. Photo: NASA, public domain

reels.hook: Even if God doesn’t save us, we still won’t bow.
reels.body: King Nebuchadnezzar set up a gold image about 90 feet tall and ordered everyone to bow down when the music played. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego wouldn’t. The furious king asked, “Who is that God that shall deliver you out of my hands?” (Daniel 3:15). They answered that God could save them. But even if He didn’t, they still would not bow. Their faith was in God, not in getting rescued.

verse.text: But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.

question.q: What did the three friends mean by “But if not”?
question.right: They’d obey God even if He didn’t save them
wrong: They’d bow down if God didn’t come first
They weren’t sure God could save them
question.why: If God didn’t deliver them, “we will not serve thy gods.” Their obedience didn’t depend on being saved.

bonus.q: In verse 16 the friends say, “We are not careful to answer thee.” How do modern translations put it, say this week’s Scripture Helps?
bonus.right: We have no need to answer you
wrong: We are afraid to answer you
bonus.why: They say it means the three had no need to answer the king. Their minds were already made up: they would not worship the image.
bonus.find: We have no need to answer you in this matter

image.alt: Old etching of crowds kneeling before King Nebuchadnezzar’s tall statue as a horn blows, while three men in long robes stand upright at the left
image.credit: The Idol of Nebuchadnezzar, by Jan Luyken, 1698. Public domain

reels.hook: Three were thrown in. The king saw one more.
reels.body: The furnace was so hot it killed the soldiers who threw the three friends in (Daniel 3:22). Then the king jumped up. He saw four men walking around in the fire, unhurt. When they came out, not a hair was singed. The king said God had “sent his angel, and delivered his servants that trusted in him” (Daniel 3:28). God didn’t keep them out of the fire. He sent help into it.

verse.text: He answered and said, Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the form of the fourth is like the Son of God.

question.q: What did the king see when he looked into the furnace?
question.why: “Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt.” Someone had come to be with them.

bonus.q: In Daniel 3:27, what had not even passed on the three men?
bonus.hunt: In Daniel 3, what had not even passed on the three men?
bonus.why: Verse 27: their coats weren’t changed, “nor the smell of fire had passed on them.” They didn’t even smell like smoke.
bonus.find: nor the smell of fire had passed on them

image.alt: Glowing slag, the melted junk drained off the top of molten steel, pouring from a steel-mill furnace
image.credit: Slag run-off at a steel mill, 1941. Photo: Alfred T. Palmer, public domain

reels.hook: The proudest king on earth learned who really rules.
reels.body: Nebuchadnezzar dreamed of a giant tree chopped down to a stump. Daniel said the tree was the king himself. A year later the king bragged about the “great Babylon, that I have built” (Daniel 4:30). That same hour he lost his mind and lived like an animal for “seven times” (Daniel 4:32). At last he looked up to heaven, his understanding came back, and he praised God.

verse.text: Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.

question.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar learn after living like an animal?
question.right: God rules and can humble the proud
wrong: Kings must be tougher on their people
question.why: He praised “the King of heaven” and said “those that walk in pride he is able to abase.” To abase means to bring low.

bonus.q: In Daniel 4:27, what did Daniel tell the king to show to the poor?
bonus.hunt: In Daniel 4, what did Daniel tell the king to show to the poor?
bonus.why: Verse 27: “break off thy sins by righteousness, and thine iniquities by shewing mercy to the poor.” Daniel hoped the king would repent in time.

image.alt: Black-and-white photo from 1932 of the crumbling brick ruins of ancient Babylon
image.credit: Babylon's ruins, 1932. Photo: Matson Collection, Library of Congress, public domain

reels.hook: A hand wrote on the wall. The king’s knees knocked.
reels.seek: God measured the king, and he came up short
reels.body: King Belshazzar threw a feast and drank from the sacred cups taken from the Lord’s temple in Jerusalem. Suddenly fingers appeared and wrote on the palace wall. Only Daniel could read it: God had numbered the king’s kingdom, weighed him, and given his kingdom away. Belshazzar knew how God had humbled Nebuchadnezzar, but he never humbled himself (Daniel 5:22). That very night Babylon fell (Daniel 5:30).

verse.text: TEKEL; Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting.

question.q: What did “Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting” mean?
question.right: God judged him and he fell short
wrong: He would have to pay heavy taxes
He had grown too heavy to ride
question.why: God had weighed the king, like goods on a scale, and he didn’t measure up. He “hast not humbled thine heart” (Daniel 5:22).

bonus.q: This week’s Scripture Helps say mene, tekel, and upharsin were also names of what?
wrong: Gods of the Medes and Persians
bonus.why: They say the three words named weights, from heaviest to lightest. That may have pictured Babylon’s power shrinking away.
bonus.find: referred to ancient units of weight, listed in descending order

image.credit: The Cyrus Cylinder, British Museum. Photo: Daderot, public domain (CC0)

reels.hook: A new law said don’t pray. Daniel opened his window.
reels.body: Jealous leaders couldn’t find anything wrong with Daniel, so they tricked King Darius into signing a law: for thirty days, ask nothing of any god or man except the king. Daniel knew. He went home, opened his windows toward Jerusalem, and knelt to pray three times a day, “as he did aforetime.” Prayer wasn’t new for Daniel. It was his habit, and he kept it, even with lions waiting.

verse.text: Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.

question.q: Why did Daniel keep praying after the law was signed?
question.right: Praying to God mattered more to him
wrong: He hadn’t heard of the new law
He wanted the king to notice him
question.why: He “knew that the writing was signed,” and still prayed “as he did aforetime.” He wouldn’t stop talking to God for anyone.

bonus.q: This week’s Scripture Helps compare Daniel’s den with Jesus’s tomb. How was the tomb closed?
bonus.right: A large stone and a Roman seal
wrong: A wooden door and an iron lock
A row of soldiers with spears
bonus.why: They say the den was sealed with a stone and the king’s seal, and Jesus’s tomb with a stone and a Roman seal. Both came out alive.
bonus.find: sealed with a large stone and a Roman seal

bonus.q: In Daniel 6:18, how did the king spend the night Daniel was in the den?
bonus.hunt: In Daniel 6, how did the king spend the night Daniel was in the den?
bonus.why: Verse 18: he “passed the night fasting,” with no music, and “his sleep went from him.” He was worried about Daniel.

image.alt: A young boy with his arms folded and his eyes closed, praying
image.credit: Prayer, from the Church Media Library

reels.hook: Not another beast this time. Someone like a man.
reels.body: After four wild beasts, Daniel saw someone very different: “one like the Son of man” coming “with the clouds of heaven.” He was given a kingdom that “shall not be destroyed” (Daniel 7:14). Jesus often called Himself the Son of Man. At His trial He used Daniel’s words about Himself, saying He would come “in the clouds of heaven” (Mark 14:62).

verse.text: I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.

question.q: Who is the “Son of man” Daniel saw coming with the clouds?
question.why: Jesus often called Himself “the Son of man.” Daniel saw Him given “an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away” (Daniel 7:14).

bonus.q: In Mark 14:62, where did Jesus say they would see the Son of man sitting?
bonus.hunt: In Mark 14, where did Jesus say they would see the Son of man sitting?
bonus.right: On the right hand of power
wrong: On a throne in the temple
bonus.why: Verse 62: “ye shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power.” Jesus used Daniel’s words about Himself.
bonus.find: sitting on the right hand of power

image.alt: Painting of Jesus Christ in a white robe and red sash coming down through the clouds with His arms open, as angels on each side blow trumpets
image.credit: The Second Coming, by Harry Anderson

reels.hook: The oldest man ever gets a seat of honor.
reels.body: Daniel saw thrones, and “the Ancient of days” sitting in judgment, with hair “like the pure wool.” Modern revelation tells us who he is: Adam, the father of all (Doctrine and Covenants 27:11). Joseph Smith taught that before the Second Coming, Adam will call his children together, and the Son of Man will come to him and receive the kingdom (Daniel 7:13–14).

verse.text: I beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool: his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire.

question.q: Who does modern revelation say the Ancient of Days is?
wrong: Enoch, of the city of Zion
question.why: The Lord speaks of “Michael, or Adam, the father of all, the prince of all, the ancient of days” (Doctrine and Covenants 27:11).

bonus.q: In Daniel 7:10, what were opened when the judgment was set?
bonus.hunt: In Daniel 7, what were opened when the judgment was set?
bonus.why: Verse 10: “the judgment was set, and the books were opened.” Thousands upon thousands stood before the Ancient of days.

image.credit: Looking over Adam-ondi-Ahman, from the Church Media Library

lines: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon takes young men from Judah to train for his court. Daniel and his three friends are given new Babylonian names. (verses 1–7)
Daniel decides not to make himself unclean with the king’s food and wine. He asks for a ten-day test of plain food and water. (verses 8–14)
After ten days they look healthier than all the others. God gives the four of them knowledge and wisdom, and Daniel understands visions and dreams. (verses 15–17)
The king finds them ten times wiser than all his magicians and astrologers, and Daniel serves in Babylon for many years. (verses 18–21)

review.about: “Make himself unclean” is defile, as the Scripture Helps explain it (to make himself spiritually unclean).
“Plain food” is the chapter heading’s; the KJV’s pulse is food made of seeds and grains (footnote 12a).
Left as “for many years”: the verse names King Cyrus, and a bonus asks for that name.

lines: King Nebuchadnezzar has a troubling dream. When his wise men can’t tell him what he dreamed, he orders all the wise men killed, Daniel too. (verses 1–13)
Daniel asks for time. He and his friends pray, God shows Daniel the secret in a night vision, and Daniel praises God. (verses 14–23)
Daniel tells the king his dream: a great metal image smashed by a stone cut out without hands. The stone is God’s latter-day kingdom, filling the earth. (verses 24–45)
The king honors Daniel’s God as the revealer of secrets and makes Daniel ruler over the province of Babylon. (verses 46–49)

review.about: “The stone is God’s latter-day kingdom” is from the chapter heading; the verses say God will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed (verse 44).

lines: King Nebuchadnezzar sets up a huge golden image and commands everyone to bow down and worship it, or be thrown into a fiery furnace. (verses 1–7)
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego refuse. They tell the king God can save them, but even if He doesn’t, they won’t worship his gods. (verses 8–18)
The king has them thrown into the furnace, heated seven times hotter. Then he sees four men walking in the fire, unharmed. (verses 19–25)
The three come out without even a burned hair. The king praises their God, because no other god can save like Him. (verses 26–30)
Nebuchadnezzar dreams of a great tree cut down. A messenger from heaven says the Most High rules over kingdoms and can set even the lowliest man over them. (verses 1–18)
Daniel explains that the tree is the king. He will live like an animal until he learns that God rules. Daniel begs him to repent. (verses 19–27)
A year later the king brags about the great Babylon he has built. He loses his mind and eats grass like an ox, as the dream said. (verses 28–33)
When his understanding returns, he praises God, the King of heaven, who rules over all and can humble the proud. (verses 34–37)

review.about: “The lowliest man” is the heading’s “basest of men” (the KJV’s word in verse 17).
The chapter is told by Nebuchadnezzar himself (verses 1–18 and 34–37); the line leaves that out to stay short.

lines: King Belshazzar throws a great feast and drinks wine from the sacred vessels taken from the temple in Jerusalem, praising idols of gold and silver. (verses 1–4)
Fingers of a hand write on the palace wall. The king is terrified, and none of his wise men can read the writing. (verses 5–9)
The queen remembers Daniel. Daniel turns down the king’s gifts and scolds him for his pride and his idols. (verses 10–24)
Daniel explains the words: God has ended the king’s reign, weighed him, and given his kingdom to the Medes and Persians. That night Babylon falls. (verses 25–31)
Darius sets Daniel over his rulers. Jealous men find no fault in him, so they trick the king into a law: for thirty days, pray only to the king. (verses 1–9)
